shortName: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
additionalCoursework: Applicants are encouraged to complete coursework or experiences which provide exposure to social determinants of health and disparities in health care outcomes. Coursework examples include sociology, public health, political science, global health, bioethics, urban studies, history, and economics.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Patricia S. Levinson Center for Multicultural and Community Affairs (CMCA) of the Mount Sinai Health System’s Office for Diversity and Inclusion is a key driver of educational excellence, for promoting a diverse physician workforce, and for advancing equitable health care for all. The CMCA advocates for and fosters an inclusive learning environment that engages diversity to strengthen and maintain a positive educational experience for all students.  The CMCA establishes and maintains networks that enable collaboration and the ability to effectively meet the diverse needs of all students. The CMCA develops programs and activities that affirm student identity, build community, and cultivate leadership, enabling all students to effectively work across communities and provide outreach to students promoting available programs, services, and other resources to meet the diverse needs of all applicants and students.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: All requests for leaves of absence are made directly to and granted at the discretion of the Office for Academic and Student Affairs. A leave of absence constitutes a mutual agreement between school and student with regard to utilization of time during the leave, as well as the requirements that must be met prior to reentering the curriculum.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student Activities at ISMMS fall under the purview of the Student Council. There are numerous student groups that cover a broad spectrum of interests including those that focus on career and professional development, recreation, community service & advocacy, and affinity groups. New York City affords extraordinary opportunities for exploring personal interests. Together the Student Council and the Office of Student Affairs help students make the most of these opportunities. The Mount Sinai Hospital recreation office also offers students discounted tickets to shows, concerts, movies, and other events. Student Affairs works with the Student Council on many community-building social events and students participate in a diversity of athletic and artistic groups. The Student Council also serves as a conduit for feedback between the student body and administration, advocating for student wellness and academic success.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The campus sits on the border between the Upper East Side of Manhattan and the thriving and vibrant community of East Harlem. Student housing is located across the street from the campus, as is Central Park. The Museum Mile, restaurants, shopping, and public transportation are all convenient to the campus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students are guaranteed modern and spacious apartments in Aron Hall, located across the street from the school. Couples and family housing is located within easy walking distance and is on a space available basis.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai’s campus is in New York City, home to a very robust LGBTQ community. The student affinity group, Stonewall Alliance, helps coordinate social events, educational programming, mentorship programs, advocacy opportunities, research, curricular reform initiatives, and community support. The entire student body is welcome.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai understands student wellness from a holistic perspective and our well-being programming encompasses a wide range of programs and resources aimed at supporting the multifaceted needs of students. During your first weeks, you will be oriented to our multi-dimensional model of wellness which encompasses nine interconnected aspects of well-being. 
-Receive frequent check-ins with your career and wellness advisors who represent key members of your support team and essential pieces of your Occupational Dimension of Wellness. 
-Support your Physical and Psychological Dimensions of Wellness through accessing our Student Health Center and Student and Trainee Mental Health Program as well as via our free 24/7 counseling and crisis phone line. 
-Participate in PEERS, a student-led well-being program, to enhance your coping skills and those of your patients through evidence-based practices all while building connections with your peers.  
-Tend to your Social and Cultural Dimensions of Wellness by engaging in student-run activities, along with a wide variety of affinity groups, that promote community building. 
-Take advantage of resources available through our Office of Student Financial Services, food pantry, free wellness item vending machine, and more to support your Financial Dimension of Wellness.  
-Experience how our student lounge, study spaces, housing options, and accessibility to Central Park enhance your Environmental Dimension of Wellness while creating a rich learning space meant to support your Intellectual Dimension of Wellness and academic success.  
-Connect with your sense of purpose and meaning by supporting your Spiritual Dimension of Wellness through access to prayer spaces and Chaplaincy Services. 
-At ISMMS, you will have access to a wide range of additional wellness resources as we support you in creating a fulfilling learning and community building experience throughout your medical education.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai fosters a campus culture that helps students achieve their maximum potential through exceptional clinical experiences, curricular initiatives, community immersion, and mentored research. At ISMMS, students apply science in the service of society- reflecting our core values. Our scientifically-based education aims to improve healthcare needs locally in New York City and around the world. We foster a supportive environment for all students and encourage their bold thinking to fundamentally drive change in medicine through innovation and collaboration.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai has a team approach for academic support programs with course and clerkship directors, peers, faculty advisors, a learning center and learning specialists.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Early clinical exposure is structured through our Practice of Medicine module, integrating classroom learning with real-life patient experiences in clinical spaces.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The educational approach emphasizes interactive and experiential learning,  collaborative sessions, large group seminars/lectures, hands-on labs, simulations, and clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Our students benefit from training at a wide range of clinical settings within our health system of network hospitals and clinics as well as our affiliated hospitals located throughout New York City.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: While attendance at selected large group lectures or seminars is not mandatory, the medical education experience is fundamentally in-person. Active participation and attendance is highly encouraged.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Icahn Mount Sinai introduces ASCEND, a transformative curriculum designed to meet the evolving demands of the medical profession within the context of a changing society. This comprehensive approach weaves together systems-based learning, hands-on clinical experiences, and cutting-edge topics like artificial intelligence, healthcare delivery science, leadership, and a deep commitment to advocacy, social justice, and health equity.  
 
The curriculum is structured around collaborative group learning, with the Phase 1 emphasizing the importance of community through learning cohorts and the guidance of longitudinal faculty facilitators. Frequent, varied assessments provide constructive feedback, while dedicated longitudinal mentorships support knowledge, clinical competency, and scholarly pursuits. This phase is enriched by early clinical exposures, offering students hands-on experiences from the outset, ensuring a seamless integration of theoretical knowledge with practical skills. 
 
Clinical clerkships in Phase 2 offer diverse experiences in acute, emergent, and chronic disease management settings, underscored by an emphasis on longitudinal clinical mentorship. Phase 3 builds upon this foundation with advanced clinical experiences, elective opportunities, and areas of concentration that include scientific discovery, advocacy, health system science, and leadership. These chosen areas encourage profound exploration of personal interests, leading to impactful scholarly projects. The phase culminates in a transition to residency, preparing students for their future roles as leaders in healthcare.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
Our curriculum is deeply integrated with primary care, particularly relevant given our location in East Harlem. Students can personalize their education by selecting a primary care field in the chronic care clerkship, making their learning experience directly applicable and meaningful.  
 
The East Harlem Health Outreach Program (EHHOP), a student-run, physician-supervised clinic, stands as a cornerstone of our community engagement opportunity efforts, addressing the comprehensive healthcare needs of East Harlem's uninsured residents. This initiative is supported by specialized satellite clinics in critical areas such as Mental Health, Women's Health, and Ophthalmology, showcasing our dedication to healthcare equity.  
 
Additional program opportunities like our Human Rights Program, Adolescent Health Center, and Transgender Medicine Program enrich our curriculum, offering students diverse experiences in primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Medical Student Research Office (MSRO) provides foundational training and oversight for students to complete a required scholarly experience as part of their graduation requirements. Through a series of integrated curricular sessions, the MSRO equips students with core skills in research methodology, study design, statistical analysis, and scholarly communication. Students receive individualized guidance from MSRO research track advisors, who assist with mentor selection and project development. Area of Concentration (AOC) directors offer additional support to help students align their scholarly work with the thematic focus of their AOC. Current AOCs include Scientific and Scholarly Discovery, Patient-Centered Advocacy, Healthcare Delivery Science, and Leadership and Professional Identity Formation. Dedicated time for scholarship and AOC-related work is built into Phase 3 of the curriculum, reinforcing our commitment to student-driven inquiry and professional development.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service and advocacy are deeply ingrained in the culture and climate of our community.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Consistent with our mission to cultivate future physicians and scientists adept in advancing clinical care and science, all students are required to produce a scholarly work of rigorous quality.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The largest health care system in New York State with affiliated sites in most communities in New York City. We serve a diverse patient population.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading in Pre-Clerkship phase is Pass/Fail. In the clerkship phase, grading is an Honors/Pass/Fail system.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
At the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (ISMMS), our approach to medical education allows students individually and collectively to achieve their maximum potential through exceptional clinical experiences, curricular initiatives, community immersion, and mentored research. Graduates apply science in the service of society- reflecting our core values. Our educational approach at Icahn Mount Sinai involves the seamless integration of curricula 
across all phases of learning and teaching, fostering an interconnected educational approach that equips our learners to adapt and cultivate lifelong learning skills. Our scientifically-based education has the goal of improving societal health care needs locally in New York City and around the world. We encourage and support the bold thinking and disciplined science that will fundamentally change the face of medicine.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai advances science, medicine, and health care delivery for the benefit of humanity through a culture of excellence, innovation, collaboration, and belonging. We conduct groundbreaking research; educate and nurture the next generation of exceptional clinicians, researchers, teachers, and leaders; and deliver the most advanced compassionate care with an unwavering commitment to health equity.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Students complete their undergraduate degree at their undergraduate college prior to matriculating
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Donald and Vera Blinken FlexMed Program offers early assurance to college sophomores from any academic area of study. If eligible, you can apply in the winter of your sophomore year of undergraduate school and will learn of your admissions decision by the summer. This program does not accelerate the timeline to medical school—rather our program allows you to ‘flex’ your intellectual, creative, humanistic, and science muscles during college. It also exempts you from taking the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT).

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks to confirm and hold acceptance
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A committee letter or packet of letters is preferred. If you do not have a pre-health adviser or committee at your school you must submit at least three and up to six letters of recommendation from people who can speak to your passion for a career in medicine and your intellectual journey: sources may include research mentors, professional or service supervisor, professors, or clinical preceptors.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: In addition to interviews, the day will include an opportunity to learn more about the community, curriculum and student experience at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two thirty-minute open file interviews with faculty and/or senior medical students.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be virtual for the 2027 application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: We offer interviews on a rolling basis from August-February and recommend all materials submitted as soon as possible. The final deadline to submit your supplemental application is November 1.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Applicants applying to the MD-PhD or Early Assurance Programs must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: International applicants are not eligible for the MD/PhD program and the Early Assurance programs.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Our MD Program Admissions Committee is committed to a holistic process that considers each applicant’s unique journey to the field of medicine. Pre-requisite courses completed at the community college level or in an online format will be considered on a case-by-case basis. If these required courses are fulfilled with community college level coursework, it is recommended for applicants to complete additional higher-level courses in related subjects at a 4-year accredited institution. It is strongly preferred that applicants complete courses taken on-site/in-person. Laboratory Sciences requirements should not be taken in an online format.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: While all MCAT scores are considered by the committee, they are taken in the context of the application as a whole.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Postbacc and graduate coursework are considered and taken in the context of the application as a whole.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Postbacc and graduate coursework are considered and taken in the context of the application as a whole.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Pre-requisite courses completed at the community college level or in an online format will be considered on a case-by-case basis. If these required courses are fulfilled with community college level coursework, it is recommended for applicants to complete additional higher-level courses in related subjects at a 4-year accredited institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may provide updates to the application using the application system. The Admissions Office welcomes updates throughout the cycle including Letters of Intent.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Our MD Program prepares students to be skilled physicians, in accordance with the Technical Standards as outlined by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education, the U.S. accrediting agency for medical schools.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (ISMMS) is committed to assisting accepted students with securing the resources needed to finance their medical education. In 2019, ISMMS launched the Enhanced Scholarship Initiative (ESI) which significantly increased the need-based scholarship program available to support medical students. The ESI provides a combination of institutional scholarships, institutional loans, and federal loans to support a student's cost of attendance that exceeds their expected family contribution. Students who do not qualify for need-based scholarships may be eligible for federal financial aid and/or private loans. All medical students with documented financial need are eligible for institutional financial support, regardless of citizenship status.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Highly Considering - accepted applicants should choose this action if they would like to remain on our incoming class list but continue to consider other options
Plan to Enroll - accepted applicants should choose this action if they would like to indicate ISMMS as one of their top 3 choices to enroll.

Accept Offer - accepted applicants should choose this option if we are their top choice but may continue to remain on waitlists of other schools. This will begin the enrollment process at our institution.
Commit to Enroll (MD-PhD) - applicants should choose this option if they are ready to commit to ISMMS. At this point applicants are required to withdraw from all other options for medical school.
Commit to Enroll (MD) - applicants should choose this option if they are ready to commit to ISMMS. At this point applicants are required to withdraw from all other options for medical school.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: Notifications are sent in March and the number of waitlist positions varies from year to year.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are encouraged to communicate via the application portal to accept their place and submit updates and letters of interest. Acceptance offers are sent until the start of orientation.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai values a rigorous undergraduate education in which the applicant has pushed themselves academically, taken upper level coursework, displayed intellectual curiosity and exhibited an academic passion. We also encourage students to complete coursework (for example sociology, public health, political science, global health, bioethics, urban studies, history, economics) or experiences that provide exposure to content about social determinants of health and disparities in healthcare outcomes.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Students are encouraged to complete Biology within 5 years of application/matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is looking for applicants who are poised to be the next generation of expert clinicians, physician advocates, physician-scientists, and medical educators. We seek those who demonstrate academic excellence, a passion for clinical medicine, and a commitment to patient communities through advocacy and scholarly endeavors. 

Commitment to clinical medicine and excellence in scholarship and advocacy, personal maturity, integrity, leadership, innovation and motivation for medicine are important factors. Academic excellence, the interview, recommendations, and an applicant's activities and pursuits are all criteria for a holistic evaluation. All applicants are considered, regardless of race, sex, color, creed, age, national origin, handicap, veteran status, marital status, or sexual orientation.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Exposure to health care, illness and suffering is an important factor in demonstrating a passion for the career of medicine.
